<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" id="Definitions_Restaurant" targetNamespace="http://example.org/bpmn/restaurant-buzzer">

  <bpmn:message id="Msg_Order" name="Meal order"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Msg_Payment" name="Payment"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Msg_Buzzer" name="Buzzer: When the buzzer rings, your dinner is ready"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Msg_BuzzerRings" name="Buzzer rings"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Msg_Call" name="Call for guest"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Msg_GuestAtHatch" name="Guest at service hatch"/>
  <bpmn:message id="Msg_Meal" name="Meal handed over"/>

  <bpmn:collaboration id="Collaboration_Restaurant" name="Restaurant buzzer process">
    <bpmn:participant id="Participant_Guest" name="Guest" processRef="Process_Guest"/>
    <bpmn:participant id="Participant_Restaurant" name="Restaurant" processRef="Process_Restaurant"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_Order" name="Place order" sourceRef="Task_PlaceOrder" targetRef="StartEvent_Order" messageRef="Msg_Order"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_Payment" name="Pay" sourceRef="Task_Pay" targetRef="Task_CollectMoney" messageRef="Msg_Payment"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_PassBuzzer" name="Pass buzzer" sourceRef="SendTask_PassBuzzer" targetRef="ReceiveTask_Buzzer" messageRef="Msg_Buzzer"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_BuzzerRings" name="Buzzer rings" sourceRef="SendTask_SetOffBuzzer" targetRef="Catch_BuzzerRings" messageRef="Msg_BuzzerRings"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_Call" name="Call guest" sourceRef="SendTask_CallGuest" targetRef="Catch_Call" messageRef="Msg_Call"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_GuestAtHatch" name="Guest at hatch" sourceRef="SendTask_GoToHatch" targetRef="Catch_GuestAtHatch" messageRef="Msg_GuestAtHatch"/>
    <bpmn:messageFlow id="MF_Meal" name="Meal handed over" sourceRef="SendTask_HandOverMeal" targetRef="Catch_ReceiveMeal" messageRef="Msg_Meal"/>
  </bpmn:collaboration>

  <bpmn:process id="Process_Guest" name="Guest" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:startEvent id="Start_Hungry" name="Guest feels hungry"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_EnterRestaurant" name="Enter restaurant"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_ChooseDish" name="Choose dish from changing meal range"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_WaitTurn" name="Wait until it is his turn"/>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="Task_PlaceOrder" name="Place order with employee" messageRef="Msg_Order"/>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="Task_Pay" name="Pay for meal" messageRef="Msg_Payment"/>
    <bpmn:receiveTask id="ReceiveTask_Buzzer" name="Receive buzzer" messageRef="Msg_Buzzer"/>
    <bpmn:eventBasedGateway id="EventGW_Guest" name="Buzzer or call?"/>
    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Catch_BuzzerRings" name="Buzzer rings">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_BuzzerRings" messageRef="Msg_BuzzerRings"/>

    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_GoToHatch" name="Go to service hatch" messageRef="Msg_GuestAtHatch"/>
    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Catch_ReceiveMeal" name="Meal handed over">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_ReceiveMeal" messageRef="Msg_Meal"/>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_EatMeal" name="Eat meal"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_Guest" name="Meal eaten"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_1" sourceRef="Start_Hungry" targetRef="Task_EnterRestaurant"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_2" sourceRef="Task_EnterRestaurant" targetRef="Task_ChooseDish"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_3" sourceRef="Task_ChooseDish" targetRef="Task_WaitTurn"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_4" sourceRef="Task_WaitTurn" targetRef="Task_PlaceOrder"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_5" sourceRef="Task_PlaceOrder" targetRef="Task_Pay"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_6" sourceRef="Task_Pay" targetRef="ReceiveTask_Buzzer"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_7" sourceRef="ReceiveTask_Buzzer" targetRef="EventGW_Guest"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_8" sourceRef="EventGW_Guest" targetRef="Catch_BuzzerRings"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_9" sourceRef="EventGW_Guest" targetRef="Catch_Call"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_10" sourceRef="Catch_BuzzerRings" targetRef="Merge_Guest"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_11" sourceRef="Catch_Call" targetRef="Merge_Guest"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_12" sourceRef="Merge_Guest" targetRef="SendTask_GoToHatch"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_13" sourceRef="SendTask_GoToHatch" targetRef="Catch_ReceiveMeal"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_14" sourceRef="Catch_ReceiveMeal" targetRef="Task_EatMeal"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="GF_15" sourceRef="Task_EatMeal" targetRef="End_Guest"/>

  <bpmn:process id="Process_Restaurant" name="Restaurant" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:laneSet id="LaneSet_Restaurant">
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_Employee" name="Employee">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>StartEvent_Order</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_EnterPOS</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_CollectMoney</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_SetUpBuzzer</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>SendTask_PassBuzzer</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_InformChef</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>SendTask_SetOffBuzzer</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Merge_Employee</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>EventGW_Hatch</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Catch_GuestAtHatch</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Timer_5Min</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>SendTask_CallGuest</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>SendTask_HandOverMeal</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>End_MealHandedOver</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_Chef" name="Chef">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_PrepareMeal</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_PlaceInHatch</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_InformEmployee</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
    </bpmn:laneSet>

    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_Order" name="Order placed by guest">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_Order" messageRef="Msg_Order"/>
    </bpmn:startEvent>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_EnterPOS" name="Enter order into POS system"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_CollectMoney" name="Collect money from guest"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_SetUpBuzzer" name="Set up buzzer"/>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_PassBuzzer" name="Pass buzzer to guest" messageRef="Msg_Buzzer"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_InformChef" name="Inform chef of new meal order"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_PrepareMeal" name="Prepare meal"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_PlaceInHatch" name="Place finished meal in service hatch"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_InformEmployee" name="Inform employee meal is in service hatch"/>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_SetOffBuzzer" name="Set off guest's buzzer" messageRef="Msg_BuzzerRings"/>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Merge_Employee" name="Waiting for guest"/>
    <bpmn:eventBasedGateway id="EventGW_Hatch" name="Guest at hatch or timeout?"/>
    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Catch_GuestAtHatch" name="Guest appears at service hatch">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_GuestAtHatch" messageRef="Msg_GuestAtHatch"/>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Timer_5Min" name="5 minutes pass">
      <bpmn:timerEventDefinition id="TED_5Min">
        <bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT5M</bpmn:timeDuration>
      </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_CallGuest" name="Call guest" messageRef="Msg_Call"/>
    <bpmn:sendTask id="SendTask_HandOverMeal" name="Hand over meal to guest" messageRef="Msg_Meal"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_MealHandedOver" name="Meal handed over"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_1" sourceRef="StartEvent_Order" targetRef="Task_EnterPOS"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_2" sourceRef="Task_EnterPOS" targetRef="Task_CollectMoney"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_3" sourceRef="Task_CollectMoney" targetRef="Task_SetUpBuzzer"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_4" sourceRef="Task_SetUpBuzzer" targetRef="SendTask_PassBuzzer"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_5" sourceRef="SendTask_PassBuzzer" targetRef="Task_InformChef"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_6" sourceRef="Task_InformChef" targetRef="Task_PrepareMeal"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_7" sourceRef="Task_PrepareMeal" targetRef="Task_PlaceInHatch"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_8" sourceRef="Task_PlaceInHatch" targetRef="Task_InformEmployee"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_9" sourceRef="Task_InformEmployee" targetRef="SendTask_SetOffBuzzer"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_10" sourceRef="SendTask_SetOffBuzzer" targetRef="Merge_Employee"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_11" sourceRef="Merge_Employee" targetRef="EventGW_Hatch"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_12" sourceRef="EventGW_Hatch" targetRef="Catch_GuestAtHatch"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_13" sourceRef="EventGW_Hatch" targetRef="Timer_5Min"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_14" sourceRef="Timer_5Min" targetRef="SendTask_CallGuest"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_15" sourceRef="SendTask_CallGuest" targetRef="Merge_Employee"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_16" sourceRef="Catch_GuestAtHatch" targetRef="SendTask_HandOverMeal"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="RF_17" sourceRef="SendTask_HandOverMeal" targetRef="End_MealHandedOver"/>
  </bpmn:process>

</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description says that a participant remains idle, pausing until a stated turn or a stated readiness of something is reached, before a following step can begin, and the description does not say that the participant performs any work during that pause: Model the pause as an intermediate catch event on the sequence flow between the preceding step and the following step, and do not model the pause as a task. Use a task only for work that the description says is actually performed during the pause.
rules.situation: the description says that a participant remains idle, pausing until a stated turn or a stated readiness of something is reached, before a following step can begin, and the description does not say that the participant performs any work during that pause

rules.instruction: When the description has a step of one role whose result is passed to a different role, and the receiving role then performs its own described step as a task in its own pool (for example, a role that is asked to act on information or an item another role has sent): Model the receiving step as a task in the receiving role's pool and draw a message flow from the sending step in the sender's pool to that receiving task, with the arrow pointing from sender to receiver. Do not replace this flow with one that ends at a catch event when the receiver's described step is a performed task, and do not reverse the arrow direction.
rules.situation: the description has a step of one role whose result is passed to a different role, and the receiving role then performs its own described step as a task in its own pool (for example, a role that is asked to act on information or an item another role has sent)

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant waits for another participant to make something available or to arrive, and then performs one or more further described actions on it in a stated order, such as picking up and then consuming the item: Model the waited-for occurrence as an intermediate catch event. Then model each described action of the participant as its own task, in the stated order, on the sequence flow after that event. Do not place an end event between the catch event and these tasks, and do not treat the occurrence itself as the completion of the process.
rules.situation: the description states that a participant waits for another participant to make something available or to arrive, and then performs one or more further described actions on it in a stated order, such as picking up and then consuming the item

rules.instruction: When the description has a participant perform two or more of its own actions on the same item in one sentence, joined by a conjunction such as 'and', after being told the item is available for it, and the generated model shows only one task or merges them into a state label: Model each action the participant performs on the item as its own task, in the order the sentence gives, after the wait for the stated availability. Label each task with the action the description states (for example, the participant takes the item, then the participant uses it). Do not merge them into one task, and do not use a catch event or an end event to stand for the action.
rules.situation: the description has a participant perform two or more of its own actions on the same item in one sentence, joined by a conjunction such as 'and', after being told the item is available for it, and the generated model shows only one task or merges them into a state label

rules.instruction: When the description says a participant performs a follow-up action, such as calling or contacting another party, only when that party does not respond within a stated time limit, possibly repeating the action several times: Model the stated time limit as an intermediate timer event on the sequence flow where the limit starts. Model the participant's follow-up action as its own task, placed on the flow after that timer and performed by that participant. Do not model the follow-up action as an intermediate catch event, and do not use an event-based or exclusive gateway to choose between the response and the follow-up unless the description states a choice between paths. If the action is repeated, route the flow back to the timer.
rules.situation: the description says a participant performs a follow-up action, such as calling or contacting another party, only when that party does not respond within a stated time limit, possibly repeating the action several times

rules.instruction: When the description states that one participant's work or the process can finish in several distinct ways, such as completing a delivered item, the participant leaving without completing the usual steps, or a party not responding, and each way is described as its own outcome: Model each distinct outcome at which the work or the process stops as its own end event, placed on the branch that leads to that outcome and named for that outcome. Include outcomes in which a participant leaves or stops early, not only the normal completion. Do not let several distinct outcomes share one end event, and do not leave a stated outcome without an end event.
rules.situation: the description states that one participant's work or the process can finish in several distinct ways, such as completing a delivered item, the participant leaving without completing the usual steps, or a party not responding, and each way is described as its own outcome

rules.instruction: When the description says an external participant, such as a person or another software system, starts the process by sending it a message, and the process sends messages back to that same participant while it runs: Model the external participant as its own pool. Inside that pool, model the sending of the initiating message as a task. Draw a message flow from that task to the message start event of the process pool. Draw a message flow from each process task that sends a message back to the external participant's pool. Do not place these sending and receiving steps inside the process pool itself.
rules.situation: the description has one participant that sends a request or order to another participant, and that receiving participant then performs its own described steps (for example preparing something at a separate place) and reports back to the sender

promoted.trigger: the description states that one participant is held until another participant makes something available or arrives, and then describes one or more further actions by the first participant on it, in a stated order
promoted.instruction: Model the awaited occurrence as an intermediate catch event. Model each described action of the participant as its own task, in the stated order, on the sequence flow after that event. Do not place an end event between the catch event and these tasks, and do not treat the occurrence itself as the completion of the process.
promoted.detail: general form of EXS-054, written after it improved the model of example 24
